headline: The US government's buying agency has issued its final contract clause on how AI language-model suppliers must safeguard government data.
score_reason: Issued 28 Sep 2026, before the edition window, and of interest mainly to contractors.
importance_line: Companies selling chatbot-type AI to federal agencies get firmer rules from 19 Oct 2026, softened from the June draft, but some industry concerns remain and GSA has not said if more clauses will follow.
summary: The Government Contracts Legal Forum reports that the General Services Administration, the agency that buys for the US government, issued its final clause on large language models (the AI behind chatbots) on 28 Sep 2026, effective 19 Oct, after a March draft that would have banned AI parts controlled by non-US entities was dropped in June. Compared with June, the final version narrows what counts as government data, narrows the 72-hour incident notice, replaces the demand for a "neutral, nonpartisan" model with a duty to use reasonable efforts to prioritise accuracy and objectivity, lets the government suspend a model at any time and caps decommissioning costs at 25 percent of the affected order, but it still overrides contractors' own commercial terms.
